opportunities.title: Constraining power and FoM3 vs survey area evaluated at each footprint's OWN adopted baryon-safe lmax, with a cost-of-safety ratio panel
opportunities.question_answered: Once you are only allowed to use baryon-safe scales, does weak-lensing constraining power still improve with survey area — or does it saturate? And how large is the price of baryon safety as a function of area?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: The paper currently shows sigma-vs-area and FoM3-vs-area at FULL resolution (lmax=1020, HOS scales1234), i.e. in the regime the paper itself declares baryon-biased. The forecast a reader actually needs is the usable one. I computed it from the surviving nulls and the answer is a genuine result the paper does not have: retained FoM3 falls monotonically with area — 0.84 / 0.55 / 0.51 / 0.42 / 0.31 / 0.21 at 2000/5000/10000/14000/28000/35000 deg^2 — and in ABSOLUTE terms the baryon-safe FoM3 saturates and even turns over (219669 at 28000 vs 206067 at 35000), because the adopted lmax shrinks faster than the area grows. sigma(S8) degrades by 1.07x at 2000 deg^2 rising to 1.83x at 35000 deg^2 (0.0167 -> 0.0307). That single sentence — 'under baryon-safe cuts, PS constraining power saturates beyond ~28000 deg^2' — is a headline-grade forecast statement, and it reframes the existing -0.46 slope figure as an upper bound rather than a forecast.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS AND VERIFIED READABLE. Null posteriors outputs/baryon_tension/ps_submean_l37/posteriors/mask_{02000,05000,10000,14000,28000,35000}/null/ at the adopted lmax 860/580/540/460/380/340 (readable seeds 4/5/5/5/5/5, each (3000,6)) and at lmax=1020 for the full-res reference (5/5/5/4/10/4). opportunities.effort_note: ~1-2 h of scripting on the login node; the numerics above took under a minute for all 12 (area, cut) cells. Run under jaxili or aname (no getdist needed — pure numpy covariance).
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: (1) Do NOT copy plot_scaling_vs_area.py's baked-in pre-crash guide constants (0.0135*(A/14000)^-0.5, 1.05e5*(A/14000)^1.5) — they no longer touch the post-damage data. opportunities.title: Recompute the 3-param tension table from the surviving posteriors AND restore the destroyed 6-param family — then show how the adopted cut depends on the tension criterion
opportunities.question_answered: Are the paper's headline adopted lmax cuts stable under the post-damage seed subset, and how much does the 'baryon-safe' cut depend on whether the 0.3-sigma tolerance is imposed on 3 or 6 parameters?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Two things at once. First, reproducibility: the campaign table records n=5 everywhere but only 36/108 cells still hold 5 pairs, and the table is currently unverifiable — I verified the recomputation path works and reproduces the shipped number bit-for-bit at the reference cell (14000@460: recomputed mean 0.28757, table 0.28757, both n=5), so a post-damage re-derivation overlaid on the archived pre-damage curve would convert the paper's largest un-checkable claim into a checked one. Second, new science: the 6-param tables were destroyed (all four ps_submean_l37 6-param CSVs are 100% NUL), and recomputing them shows the criterion matters enormously — at 14000 the 6-param Q_DM is 0.033 sigma where the 3-param is 0.288, and it only crosses 0.3 sigma near lmax~600 instead of 480. So the paper's adopted 460 is a conservative choice driven by the 3-param projection, and saying so (with the 6-param curve shown) pre-empts an obvious referee question about why the tolerance is imposed on a subspace.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS. All ps_submean_l37 / ps_fullsky_l37 / bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37 posteriors are (3000,6) arrays carrying all six parameters, so both projections are computable. Estimator already written: scripts/tension/estimators.py (q_dm_tension, SUBSET_INDICES=(0,1,2), PARAM_NAMES, TRUTH) works under the aname interpreter — 10 Q_DM evaluations took 1.2 s, so the full 108-cell x 5-seed x 2-projection sweep is ~5 min. Surviving reference: tension_3param_agg.csv and tension_3param_long.csv (541 lines) are intact for the before/after comparison.
opportunities.effort_note: Half a day: one sweep script writing a new long+agg table (do NOT write into the campaign tables/ dir) plus a two-panel figure. aname interpreter; 34 s of that is the tensiometer import.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: NEVER write into outputs/baryon_tension/*/tables/ — scripts/monitor_tension_pilot.py already overwrites tension_3param_agg.csv and that file is the ONLY surviving record of the full-seed campaign. Archive it read-only first and write the re-derivation to a new directory. Scientifically: a 6-param Gaussian Q_DM from 3000 NPE samples has a noisier 6x6 covariance than the 3x3 case, and chi2(6) dilutes a fixed 0.3-sigma threshold, so the 6-param curve must be presented as 'the same tolerance is a weaker requirement in more dimensions', not as evidence that higher lmax is safe. Also record which seeds entered each cell — the two existing sidecars use n_seeds with opposite (pre- vs post-damage) meanings, and this figure must pick one and say which.

opportunities.title: Refined step-20 tension curve at the reference footprint: how big is the safety margin, really?
opportunities.question_answered: On the finer multipole grid that exists only at 14000 deg^2, where exactly does the baryon bias cross 0.3 sigma, and how much headroom does the adopted cut actually have?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Footprint 14000 uniquely carries a step-20 lmax grid (36 cuts, 340..1024) that nobody has ever plotted — every figure uses the step-40 subset. I computed the dense curve: 420 -> 0.193, 440 -> 0.296, 460 -> 0.288, 480 -> 0.480, 500 -> 0.413. Two publishable consequences. (a) The adopted cut stays 460, which is reassuring, but the first FAILING cut is 480, not 500 — so the true safety margin at the reference footprint is 20 multipoles, not the 40 the step-40 grid implies, and the paper should quote it that way. (b) The curve is locally non-monotonic (440 above 460, 480 above 500) at the ~0.05-sigma level, which is direct evidence that seed noise, not signal, sets the crossing resolution — exactly the caveat that makes the crossing-vs-largest-safe distinction (commit 4bc76a3) matter.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS AND ENUMERATED. outputs/baryon_tension/ps_submean_l37/posteriors/mask_14000/{null,biased}/ at every 20-multipole step; matched-pair counts I measured: 340:5, 360:5, 380:5, 400:3, 420:5, 440:3, 460:5, 480:4, 500:5, 520:2, 540:4, 560:4, 580:5, 600:1, 620:1, then 640..1024 mostly 3-5 with two thin cells (980:1, 1024:1). Same estimator as above.

opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Cells 600, 620, 980 and 1024 retain a single pair and MUST be drawn with a distinct marker or omitted — a one-seed point plotted like a five-seed point is how the 2.22-sigma headline problem happened in the first place. Do not use the dense grid to claim a refined adopted cut at other footprints: the step-20 grid exists ONLY at 14000, so this is a resolution check at one footprint, not a re-derivation of the cut ladder.

opportunities.title: Null-arm accuracy: is the NPE posterior actually centred on truth, at the level of the 0.3-sigma tolerance?
opportunities.question_answered: How far from the true input cosmology does each null (nobaryons-vs-nobaryons) posterior sit, in units of its own width — and is that offset larger than the baryon effect the paper is trying to measure?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: There is currently NO calibration evidence anywhere for the corrected posteriors (see the TARP item below: 0 of the 77 surviving coverage datasets is submean/l37/r10), and a tension claim from an uncalibrated posterior is not defensible. This figure is the cheapest honest substitute and it is computable today from data already on disk. I measured it at the adopted cuts: the PS null mean is offset from truth by (Om, S8, w0) = (-0.29, +0.27, -0.22) sigma at 2000 deg^2 growing to (-0.64, +0.54, -0.26) at 28000 and (-0.62, +0.51, -0.33) at 35000; peaks at 14000 are off by -0.67 sigma in w0. Meanwhile the between-seed scatter of that mean is only 0.04-0.11 sigma, so the offset is a systematic, not noise. That is a substantive, quotable statement — the null arms sit up to ~0.6 sigma off truth, twice the 0.3-sigma baryon tolerance — and it independently corroborates the docs' 'raw NPE nulls sit off truth (S8~0.85 not 0.84)' claim that currently rests on a destroyed figure. It also explains why differencing two arms is the right estimator: a common offset cancels, and the paper should say that explicitly rather than leave it implicit.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS, ALREADY COMPUTED ABOVE. Null posteriors for PS (ps_submean_l37, all 6 footprints, adopted and full-res cuts), peaks scales1234-submean (7-10 readable seeds per footprint) and L1 scales1234-submean (6-10). Truth vector is already in the repo: scripts/tension/estimators.py TRUTH = (0.26, 0.84, -1.0, 67.36, 0.9649, 0.0493). No getdist, no tensiometer — mean/std only, so any interpreter works.
opportunities.effort_note: ~2 h including sidecars. Pure numpy; whole computation ran in seconds for 6 footprints x 3 statistics.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: This is NOT coverage: a mean-offset-over-width statistic says nothing about the tails or the credible-interval calibration, so it must be labelled 'accuracy of the posterior centre' and must not be captioned as validating the posteriors. Second, the offset is measured against a SINGLE fiducial data vector realisation, so part of it is the noise realisation rather than the estimator — say so, and quote the between-seed scatter alongside (which I measured as 0.04-0.11 sigma, i.e. the offset is not seed noise). Third, peaks at 2000 deg^2 is an outlier with 0.65-sigma between-seed scatter in Om; investigate rather than average it in silently.

opportunities.title: Per-parameter decomposition of the baryon bias, replacing the 3-param Q_DM scalar
opportunities.question_answered: WHICH cosmological parameter does baryonic feedback actually bias, in what direction, and by how much — as a function of scale cut and footprint?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Every tension figure in the repo collapses the bias to one number (Q_DM over Om, S8, w0) and one threshold. A reader cannot tell from any current figure whether the failure at lmax>460 is an S8 shift, a w0 shift, or a degeneracy-direction rotation — which is precisely what a follow-up survey analysis needs in order to decide whether to cut scales or to marginalise over a feedback parameter. All inputs are the same posteriors already used, so this is a projection of existing data, not new data: per parameter, (mean_biased - mean_null)/sigma_null versus lmax, six footprint panels, plus the unit shift vector in the (Om, S8, w0) plane to show whether the bias direction is scale-independent (a single nuisance direction, marginalisable) or rotates with lmax (not marginalisable). Either outcome is a real result, and the second would materially strengthen the argument that scale cuts are necessary.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS. Matched null/biased pairs in outputs/baryon_tension/ps_submean_l37/posteriors/ — at the adopted cuts I verified readable pairs of 4/4/4/5/4/5 (2000..35000); the full step-40 grid gives 87/108 cells with >=3 pairs. Peaks and L1 scales1234-submean pairs (5-10 per footprint) give the higher-order companion panels. BNT bin-1 pairs available too (bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37).
opportunities.effort_note: ~2-3 h. No tensiometer needed for the shift/sigma version; if you also want per-parameter 1-D Q_DM, reuse q_dm_tension with a single index.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Per-parameter shifts do not add in quadrature to the 3-param Q_DM (the parameters are strongly correlated), so the panels must not be presented as a decomposition that sums to the headline number — label them as marginal shifts and put the 3-param Q_DM on the same axis for reference. Pair matching must be by run id, not by count: several cells have unequal null/biased survivor sets and a naive min(n_null, n_biased) mispairs seeds.

opportunities.title: PS vs higher-order degeneracy directions in the CORRECTED convention at the paper's masked footprints
opportunities.question_answered: Do peak counts and the L1 norm really carry an Om-w0 degeneracy of opposite sign to the power spectrum, in the submean/l37 analysis and on the actual survey footprints — not just in a full-sky Fisher forecast?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: The opposite-sign w0 degeneracy (PS -0.38, peaks +0.72, L1 +0.82) is one of the paper's most interesting physical claims, and its only figure — outputs/diagnostics/ps_vs_hos_degeneracies.png — is orphaned: no script in scripts/, src/ or notebooks/ writes that path, so it cannot be sidecarred or re-derived, and the numbers behind it are Fisher and FULL SKY. The same quantity is directly measurable from posteriors that exist, in the corrected convention, at all six masked footprints, with 5-10 seeds per point: the (Om, w0) correlation coefficient and principal-axis angle per statistic per footprint, with seed error bars. That converts an unaccountable pixel-only figure into a provenance-compliant NPE measurement and simultaneously extends the claim from full sky to the survey footprints, where it has to hold for the combination argument to matter.
opportunities.inputs_needed: EXISTS. Null posteriors: PS ps_submean_l37 (any cut; do it at both full-res and the adopted cut), peaks scales1234-submean (7-10 readable per footprint), L1 scales1234-submean (6-10). All (3000,6). Cross-check target: outputs/diagnostics/constraining_power/fisher_contours_values.csv + _covariance.csv (intact, with sidecars) for the full-sky Fisher comparison.
opportunities.effort_note: ~2-3 h. Pure covariance algebra on files already loaded by plot_fom_vs_area.py; no getdist.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: A posterior correlation coefficient is not a Fisher degeneracy direction — NPE contours include training scatter and (per the contours_three_stats sidecar) pooling seeds inflates width, so quote per-seed correlations with a spread, not a pooled single number. Do not claim the resulting complementarity implies a specific joint-constraint gain: there is no PS+HOS joint posterior on disk (I checked — no combined-vector posterior exists anywhere in outputs/samples), so any 'gain from combining' must come from the Fisher combined vector with its documented matched-binning caveat, not from multiplying two NPE posteriors as if independent.

opportunities.title: Cost of the baryon-safe WAVELET cut for peak counts (scales1234 -> scales234 / scales2345), null-arm only
opportunities.question_answered: What does dropping the finest starlet scale cost in constraining power for peak counts, per footprint?

But a CONSTRAINING-POWER figure needs only nulls, and I verified the scales234-submean NULLS are readable at 2001, 5001, 10001 AND 14001 — including the reference footprint that the pair-based inventory reports as unusable. scales2345-submean nulls are readable at ALL SIX footprints. Use the scales1234 seed spread as the error bar on the ratio. Also: scales2345 KEEPS the coarse/mass-sheet scale, so it is not a substitute for scales234 — the coarse band is the only one sensitive to the monopole the whole submean correction exists to remove. Report them as three separate cuts, never silently swap 2345 in for 234.

And any peaks-submean posterior produced before commit b91af33 is suspect (the peaks NPE runner lacked the NaN-retry fix and can report a collapsed posterior as successful), so retrain rather than reuse.

opportunities.title: Joint PS + higher-order posterior at the reference footprint under baryon-safe cuts
opportunities.question_answered: What do you actually gain by combining the power spectrum at its adopted lmax with a baryon-safe higher-order statistic — measured with a real joint posterior rather than a Fisher forecast?
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: The paper's complementarity argument (opposite-sign w0 degeneracies, super-additive Fisher w0: sigma(w0) 0.070 PS-alone -> 0.036 with L1) rests entirely on a FULL-SKY Fisher calculation with a deliberately coarsened matched binning, plus three-statistic contours that are shown side by side but never combined. A joint NPE on the concatenated PS+HOS vector at 14000 deg^2, at the adopted PS lmax and scales234, would be the paper's strongest single result — and it is the natural companion to the baryon-safe FoM-vs-area figure in item 1. It is worth listing precisely because it is the highest-value thing that is NOT available now.
opportunities.inputs_needed: NOT AVAILABLE AS POSTERIORS — I verified no combined/joint PS+HOS posterior exists anywhere under outputs/samples or outputs/baryon_tension. Training inputs DO exist and are readable in stage3_forecast (the submean PS grids, the 28 submean L1 grids and 56 submean fiducials covering nobaryons and baryonified at all six footprints), so this is a training run, not a data problem. The missing L1 scales234-submean run (item 7) is a prerequisite for the baryon-safe version; scripts/jz/npe_hos_baryonsafe_14000.slurm already covers part of it (A100, ~20 trainings, ~20 h).
opportunities.effort_note: One long A100 campaign (20 h class), ideally combined with the peaks scales234-submean re-runs and the coverage job above so the joint result ships calibrated.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: A concatenated vector must share ONE noise realisation and one footprint mask across the two statistics, or the joint posterior inherits an artificial independence and overstates the gain — this is the same trap the Fisher work handles with a deliberately coarser matched binning, and the standalone-vs-combined binning must not be conflated (doing so inflates the apparent HOS gain). Do not approximate the joint by multiplying the two existing marginal posteriors: PS and HOS are measured on the same maps and are strongly correlated, so the product is not a valid joint and would produce a spuriously tight contour. Finally, a joint vector needs its own scale-cut derivation — the PS cut is in multipoles and the HOS cut is a wavelet scale, so 'baryon-safe' for the pair is a new measurement, not the intersection of two old ones.

data_driven.summary:
I started from the inventory and verified every claim I make below on disk, recomputing where it was cheap. Ten opportunities: eight are computable on the login node from data that already exists (I ran the core numerics for five of them), two need GPU and are marked unavailable.

The single most valuable missing result is the baryon-safe version of the paper's own area-scaling figure. The paper shows sigma-vs-area and FoM3-vs-area at full resolution — the regime it elsewhere declares baryon-biased. Evaluating the same quantities at each footprint's OWN adopted lmax (860/580/540/460/380/340), which I did from the surviving nulls, gives a new and quotable result: retained FoM3 falls monotonically with area (0.84, 0.55, 0.51, 0.42, 0.31, 0.21 from 2000 to 35000 deg^2), sigma(S8) degrades from 1.07x to 1.83x, and the absolute baryon-safe FoM3 saturates and turns over between 28000 and 35000 deg^2. In other words, under baryon-safe scale cuts, power-spectrum constraining power stops improving with survey area — a headline-grade forecast statement the paper does not currently make, and one that reframes the existing -0.46 slope as an upper bound. Null posteriors at all six adopted cuts are readable (4/5/5/5/5/5 seeds), and scripts/diagnostics/plot_fom_vs_area.py is one function away from producing it.

Second, the destroyed 6-param tension family is recoverable and scientifically interesting. Every posterior is a (3000,6) array, scripts/tension/estimators.py works under aname, and 10 Q_DM evaluations take 1.2 s — so the whole 108-cell sweep is minutes. I validated the path: recomputing 3-param Q_DM at 14000@460 from the five surviving pairs reproduces the shipped table exactly (0.28757 vs 0.28757). The same recomputation restores the 6-param family (all four masked 6-param CSVs are 100% NUL) and reveals that the adopted cut is strongly criterion-dependent: 6-param Q_DM at 14000@460 is 0.033 sigma against the 3-param 0.288, crossing 0.3 sigma only near lmax~600. The paper's 460 is a conservative 3-param projection and should be presented as such.

Third, the step-20 grid that exists only at 14000 has never been plotted. I computed it: 440 -> 0.296, 460 -> 0.288, 480 -> 0.480. The adopted cut survives, but the first failing cut is 480, not 500, so the real safety margin at the reference footprint is 20 multipoles rather than 40 — and the local non-monotonicity shows seed noise sets the crossing resolution.

Fourth, and this is the one I would not skip: there is no calibration evidence for the corrected analysis at all. All 77 surviving TARP datasets are l30/r100 or non-submean; zero carry the submean token. A CPU-only surrogate is available today, and I ran it — the null-arm posterior mean sits off truth by (-0.29,+0.27,-0.22) sigma at 2000 deg^2 rising to (-0.64,+0.54,-0.26) at 28000, with peaks off by -0.67 sigma in w0 at 14000, while between-seed scatter is only 0.04-0.11 sigma. So these are systematic offsets roughly twice the 0.3-sigma tolerance, cancelling only because the estimator differences two arms. That deserves an appendix figure and it costs an afternoon. Real TARP/SBC still needs GPU, and note the score route is half-blocked: compressed_nonbnt_460_14000.npz is BadZipFile while the bnt_580 twin loads, so the score-side coverage could only be built without its control.

Also worth building now: per-parameter bias decomposition instead of the 3-param scalar (matched pairs exist at every adopted cut); PS-vs-HOS degeneracy directions measured from corrected masked posteriors, which would give the orphaned ps_vs_hos_degeneracies.png a real generator and extend a full-sky Fisher claim to the survey footprints; the peaks baryon-safe wavelet-cut cost, where I found the scales234-submean NULLS readable at 14001 even though the tension pair is gone (a constraining-power figure needs only nulls — the pair-based inventory understates what is possible); and a compact lmax_safe(A) scaling law.

Two cautions that apply to all of it: never write into outputs/baryon_tension/*/tables/, since tension_3param_agg.csv is the only surviving record of the full-seed campaign and monitor_tension_pilot.py overwrites it; and read every CSV defensively, because 38 of them are correctly sized and 100% NUL, and pandas returns an empty frame without raising.

Every PS TARP is the pre-correction `l30-*_r100` family; every L1 TARP lacks the submean token; and `ls outputs/plots | grep -i tarp | grep -ci peak` = 0, so peak counts have NO coverage test in ANY convention. `find outputs/baryon_tension/{ps_submean_l37,bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37,ps_fullsky_l37} -iname '*calib*' -o -iname '*tarp*' -o -iname '*sbc*'` returns nothing. opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Turns 'we measured a 0.3 sigma baryon bias' from an assertion into a validated measurement. Every downstream number (adopted cuts, area scaling, three-stat contours) inherits its credibility from this one test.

opportunities.title: Null-on-truth vs lmax, per footprint — and an honest QA table to replace the 10-row one
opportunities.question_answered: Does the nobaryons null posterior actually sit on truth? If the null is itself biased, a difference-of-means tension is measuring two biased estimates against each other.
opportunities.inputs_needed: Surviving null posteriors under outputs/baryon_tension/ps_submean_l37/posteriors/mask_*/null/ (1836 .npy, 95 MB total). Needs a damage guard: bare np.load raises ValueError on the stripe-damaged members (I hit one at 14000/lmax1020).
opportunities.effort_note: I computed it in seconds. At the reference point (14000 deg^2, adopted lmax=460, n=5 clean pairs) the null sits at Omega_m 0.2500, S8 0.8557, w0 -1.0227 against truth (0.26, 0.84, -1.0): offsets of -0.58, +0.48, -0.28 sigma. The baryon shift being measured is +0.31, -0.74, -1.01 sigma. So in Omega_m the estimator's own null bias is roughly TWICE the baryon shift and of OPPOSITE sign. Two compounding defects: (a) scripts/tension/qa.py line 29 sets NULL_TRUTH_NSIGMA = 5.0, so the gate that PLAN_tension_submean_l37 §4.1(b) describes as catching 'a biased null signals a failed fit, not physics' tolerates a null bias 16x larger than the effect measured — and the same doc at line 112 argues the perm-mean observation 'justifies a tight QA null-on-truth tolerance', so the implementation contradicts its own stated rationale; (b) the campaign's QA evidence is a 519-byte, 10-row qa_report.csv covering ONE area (28000) and ONE cut (1020), while PLAN_tension_submean_l37 line 360 claims '1080 posteriors -> 1080/1080 OK, clean report'. qa/failures.csv is 76 bytes of 100% NUL.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Pre-empts the most damaging referee question. The honest framing is available and defensible: Q_DM is a difference of means, so a null bias COMMON to both arms cancels — but that has to be shown per footprint and per cut, not assumed, and here the bias is demonstrably not common across parameters.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Publishing the '1080/1080 QA OK' sentence with a 10-row table on disk. If a referee asks for the QA record, the answer is currently 10 rows and a NUL file.

opportunities.title: Constraining-power COST of the adopted scale cut (sigma and FoM3 vs lmax)
opportunities.question_answered: What does baryon safety cost? Every existing figure shows only bias removal, never the information sacrificed to achieve it.
opportunities.inputs_needed: Same surviving null posteriors. Note the campaign tables CANNOT supply this: tension_3param_agg.csv columns are exactly area,upper_cut,mean,std,n,n_total,n_excluded — nsigma only, no sigma, no FoM.
opportunities.effort_note: I computed it at 14000 deg^2 in seconds. Going from lmax 1020 to the adopted 460: sigma(Omega_m) 0.0133 -> 0.0173 (+30%), sigma(S8) 0.0238 -> 0.0326 (+37%), sigma(w0) 0.0770 -> 0.0819 (+6%), FoM3 41055 -> 21618 — a factor 1.90, i.e. the baryon-safe cut throws away 47% of the 3-parameter figure of merit. That number appears nowhere in the repo or the docs. The natural figure is a twin-axis or twin-panel version of nsigma_vs_lmax with FoM3(lmax) overlaid and the adopted cut marked on both.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: This is the actual scientific result a Stage-IV reader wants: not 'baryons bias you' but 'the mitigation costs you half your FoM, which is why BNT/compression is worth pursuing'. It also gives the BNT and score sections their motivation quantitatively instead of rhetorically.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Quoting sigma from POOLED seeds (which mixes training scatter into the width) rather than the mean of per-seed sigmas. I used the per-seed mean; pooling would inflate the apparent cost. Also lmax 860 and 1020 at 14000 have one damaged run each (n=4), so the no-cut end of the curve rests on 4 seeds and must be labelled.

opportunities.title: Sensitivity of the adopted cuts to the 0.3 sigma tolerance (and a source for the 0.3)
opportunities.question_answered: Why 0.3 sigma, and would the paper's headline lmax table survive a referee who prefers 0.2 or 0.5?
opportunities.inputs_needed: The shipped tension_3param_agg.csv alone (108 rows, intact, NULfrac 0.000).
opportunities.effort_note: I grepped PAPER_NOTES, PLAN_tension_submean_l37 and HANDOFF_JZ_PAPER_FIGURES: 0.3 sigma is used as a given everywhere and is never derived, cited, or varied. I computed the adopted-cut table across tolerances and the answer is REASSURING, which is exactly why it should be shown: tol=0.2 -> 780/540/460/420/340/340; 0.25 -> 860/580/460/420/380/340; 0.3 -> 860/580/540/460/380/340 (reproducing the paper's adopted values exactly, confirming commit 4bc76a3's largest-safe-cut rule); 0.4 -> 940/620/540/460/380/380; 0.5 -> 1020/700/580/500/420/380. At 14000 the cut moves only 420->500 across a factor 2.5 in tolerance, i.e. +/- one 40-ell step around 460. A small inset or a second row of the crossings CSV closes this.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Converts an arbitrary-looking threshold into a demonstrated robustness statement, and does it with data already on disk and already sidecarred.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Deriving the table from the crossing rather than the largest-safe cut. My reproduction only matched the paper's 860/580/540/460/380/340 because I used the largest cut with mean < tol; the first-failing cut is +40 in every case and would shift the whole table.

opportunities.title: Validate Gaussian Q_DM against the posteriors' actual non-Gaussianity
opportunities.question_answered: Is the tension estimator itself trustworthy? Q_DM assumes both posteriors are Gaussian; the paper never checks that.
opportunities.inputs_needed: Surviving posterior pairs at the adopted cuts, plus tensiometer's non-Gaussian parameter-shift estimator in the aname env. scripts/tension/estimators.py already has the dispatch hook (`estimator=` argument, docstring: 'a non-Gaussian parameter-shift estimator can be slotted in later without touching callers').
opportunities.effort_note: Partly self-documented as missing — estimators.py names the gap — but grep for exact_parameter_shift / Q_UDM / Q_DMAP across scripts/ and docs/ returns nothing, so no doc records it as a caveat on the RESULT. I measured the actual non-Gaussianity at 14000/460: S8 skew +0.135 to +0.317, w0 skew -0.133 to -0.411, |excess kurtosis| <= 0.4, with the same skew SIGN in the null and biased arms (so it largely cancels in a difference of means — the defensible argument, currently unmade). I also ran the estimator's own noise floor as a positive control: seed-pair Q_DM within the null arm is 0.002-0.005 sigma and within the biased arm 0.002-0.011 sigma, against the matched null-vs-biased 0.288 sigma (mean of 0.248/0.283/0.355/0.292/0.259) — a ~100x margin, and it reproduces the shipped table's 0.28757 at n=5 exactly. So training scatter does NOT contaminate Q_DM; the open question is purely the Gaussian approximation.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: A one-panel Gaussian-vs-non-Gaussian nsigma comparison at the six adopted cuts either confirms the whole tension axis or reveals a systematic — and the measured skew is small enough that the likely outcome is confirmation, which is a cheap win.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Non-Gaussian shift estimators need far more samples than 3000x6 to be stable in 3D and will silently return an overconfident number if under-sampled. Report the estimator's own convergence (e.g. vs sample subsets) alongside, or the cure is worse than the disease.

opportunities.title: Baryon-model dependence: the entire result rests on ONE baryonification prescription
opportunities.question_answered: Is 'baryons bias S8 by 0.74 sigma and you must cut at lmax 460' a statement about baryons, or about one prescription with one set of parameters?
opportunities.inputs_needed: A second baryonification (different prescription or varied baryon parameters) run through the full map -> MASTER/starlet -> NPE chain. Nothing on disk supports it.
opportunities.effort_note: Verified adversarially and the answer is stark: stage3_forecast carries exactly one baryon tag (`ls | grep -o 'baryonified[a-zA-Z0-9_]*'` -> 222 files, all bare 'baryonified'), and grep for bacco|TNG|mead|hmcode|Arico|Schneider|dmo|agn|wdm across the data tree returns nothing. Grepping PAPER_NOTES.md and docs/README.md for baryonification|baryon model|M_c|theta_ej returns NOTHING — the model dependence is not even flagged as a caveat, let alone addressed. This is the one gap where I would push back on the paper's framing rather than ask for compute: with a single prescription the honest claim is 'for THIS baryonification, the required cut is X', and the adopted-lmax table is a prescription-conditional result, not a survey requirement.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: A referee will not accept a scale-cut recommendation derived from one baryon model. Reframing costs nothing and is defensible; a second model would be a genuinely new result. The cheapest partial mitigation available today: use the intact baryonic_impact_*.pdf / .pkl suppression measurements in stage3_forecast to place this prescription's Cl suppression amplitude (the +0.5/+1.0/+1.5/+1.6% high-ell figures from BNT_on_spectra §5) against the published spread of hydro simulations, and state how the adopted lmax would scale with suppression amplitude.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Presenting the adopted-lmax table as a survey requirement. If the true baryon suppression is 2x this prescription's, every cut in the table is too permissive — and the paper currently has no sentence protecting against that reading.

opportunities.title: Fisher-vs-NPE reconciliation currently rests on a figure that reads no data at all
opportunities.question_answered: Why does the Fisher say BNT buys 0.45-0.48 in area while the NPE says 0.79, and is that difference measured or asserted?
opportunities.inputs_needed: A saved ladder table. The Fisher legs that survive: cov_rebinned_full_*.npz (6 files, clean) and fisher_fom_table.json + fisher_fom_table_PRECRASH_REFERENCE.json. All seven bar values are literals (0.346, 0.370, 0.484, 0.455, 0.439, 0.716), the 'NPE = 0.79' axvline is a literal, the 0.44-0.50 'true information' axvspan is a literal, and the conclusion is in the title. opportunities.title: Covariance sensitivity: the project's own validation suite stops one phase short of it
opportunities.question_answered: Are 200 fiducial perms enough for the Fisher covariance, and does the Gaussian-likelihood Fisher agree with a full posterior?
opportunities.inputs_needed: N_perm subsampling of the surviving cov_rebinned_full_*.npz plus the intact fiducial arrays (200x383 per bin/footprint, all readable).
opportunities.effort_note: Partly documented, and the docs are good here — PLAN_fisher_proper is explicit that Hartlap de-biases but misses the tails, that Sellentin-Heavens is the right tool, that Hartlap is 'the wrong tool here', and that the NPE never inverts a 200-sample covariance so the finite-N penalty does not apply to it. Those caveats are already handled; I am not re-raising them. What is NOT done: the doc's own validation list item 6, 'Convergence of sigma vs binning and (for the sim cross-checks) vs N_perm/N_realization', and items 4-5, the MCMC equivalence test, are both assigned to Phase IV — and Phases I and II/III each carry a 'RESULT' section while Phase IV carries none. So 200-perm adequacy is asserted by construction, never measured. A sigma-vs-N_perm curve (subsample 50/100/150/200 perms, plot Fisher sigma and the FoM3 ratio) is a cheap CPU job on clean inputs.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: It closes the referee's covariance question with the project's own stated criterion rather than leaving a named validation item unexecuted, and it directly tests whether the 0.72 Percival leg of the ladder is a real penalty or an artifact of stopping at 200.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Subsampling perms that are not independent. The docs report perm-perm correlation mean -0.005, so independence is established — cite it rather than re-deriving, and keep the same rebinning throughout or the binning and N_perm effects will be confounded.

opportunities.title: Score-campaign calibration is graded against the looser of two thresholds in the same repo, and its ECP curves are partly destroyed
opportunities.question_answered: Does the paper's most defensible BNT figure actually pass calibration, by the project's own standard?
opportunities.inputs_needed: The two surviving calibration.csv files (bnt_ps_bin1_score_l37/area14000/tables/ and ps_cutall_score_l37/area14000/tables/), 17-18 rows each.
opportunities.effort_note: Genuinely good news first: these DO exist, per cut, with TARP and SBC, and they are the only calibration anywhere in the corrected analysis. But three problems. (1) TWO thresholds coexist: PLAN_score_bnt_tension_14000 line 84 uses TARP max|ecp-alpha| < 0.15, while PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2 lines 124-125 uses <= 0.05 PASS / > 0.10 FAIL. Every score row sits between 0.064 and 0.090 — comfortable under 0.15, but in the INCONCLUSIVE band under the stricter rule, and not a PASS by it at any cut. The CSV stamps 'OK' regardless. (2) PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2 §8b requires inspecting the CURVE, not the scalar; I found 7 of 39 calibration_run*.json are 100% NUL, and they include ps_cutall_score_l37 cut420/cut460/cut500 — precisely the non-BNT adopted-cut region — so the curve backing the surviving scalar is gone exactly where it matters. opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: A single stated calibration criterion applied uniformly is the difference between 'calibrated' meaning something and meaning nothing. Right now a reader cannot tell which standard any 'OK' refers to.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Adopting the 0.15 threshold silently because it is the one that passes. If the strict 0.05/0.10 rule is the project's real standard (it is the one used to gate VMIM), then the score figure needs the deep-ensemble treatment VMIM got, not a relabelled threshold.

opportunities.title: 6-parameter tension is unauditable — all four 6-param tables are 100% NUL
opportunities.question_answered: Is the baryon bias an artifact of projecting onto (Omega_m, S8, w0), or does it survive in the full 6-parameter space?
opportunities.inputs_needed: Surviving posterior pairs (they carry all 6 columns — I confirmed shape (3000, 6)) plus scripts/tension/estimators.py with indices=None.
opportunities.effort_note: I byte-checked every CSV in ps_submean_l37/tables/: tension_3param_agg.csv and tension_3param_long.csv are clean (NULfrac 0.000), but tension_6param_{agg,long,pivot_mean,pivot_std}.csv AND tension_3param_{pivot_mean,pivot_std}.csv are ALL 100% NUL at correct byte size. Recomputing 6-param Q_DM from the surviving posteriors is cheap and would restore it.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Subset choice is a standard referee probe on any tension metric. Showing the 6-param curve alongside (and explaining why the 3-param is the headline) removes the suspicion of a favourable projection.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Running scripts/monitor_tension_pilot.py against this campaign to 'regenerate the tables'. It REWRITES tension_3param_agg.csv, and post-damage it would re-aggregate over the thinned seed subset — silently moving the adopted lmax values that are the paper's headline result and destroying the only surviving full-seed record. Archive the table before touching anything in that directory.

opportunities.title: Data-realization scatter of the tension is structurally absent (observation = 200-perm mean)
opportunities.question_answered: How likely is a real survey to see this bias? The quoted nsigma has no distribution over data realizations, so the 0.3 sigma threshold is a deterministic bias measure, not a detection significance.
opportunities.inputs_needed: Re-evaluating the trained flows on multiple independent perm-mean (or single-realization) observations. No flow checkpoints survive for this campaign, so this means retraining.
opportunities.effort_note: This one IS documented and correctly reasoned — run_npe_inference_auto_cross_ps_master.py line 560 takes fid_mean = np.mean(fid_full, axis=0) over the 200 perms, and PLAN_tension_submean_l37 line 110-112 states 'Observation = perm mean ... a fixed, approximately noiseless target, identical across runs ... confirms O1 (training-only scatter)'. So the authors know the error bars are training scatter. What is missing is the consequence being shown or captioned: the +/- bars on the paper's core figure are NPE training scatter, and a reader will read them as measurement uncertainty. My seed-pair control quantifies how small the training component is (null-null Q_DM 0.002-0.005 sigma) — which is reassuring for the estimator but makes the error bars nearly meaningless as uncertainty on a survey's expected bias. Minimum fix without compute: caption every nsigma figure 'error bars = NPE training-seed scatter at a fixed noise-averaged observation; they do not include data-realization scatter'.
opportunities.why_it_strengthens_the_paper: Prevents the most likely misreading of the central figure and makes the 0.3 sigma line honest — it is a threshold on a systematic bias, which is the right thing to threshold, and saying so is stronger than leaving it ambiguous.
opportunities.risk_if_done_wrong: Adding data-realization scatter by bootstrapping the 200 perms into the observation while leaving the trained flow fixed. That would produce a scatter that is too small by construction (the flow was trained for a single-realization likelihood) and would look like a rigorous error bar.

referee.summary:
I refereed the figure set against the seven demands and checked each on disk rather than reasoning from the inventories. Three findings are, in my view, blocking; several of the demands turn out to be cheap wins sitting on intact data; and two are already documented and I am not re-raising them.

BLOCKING 1 — the paper's headline campaign has no calibration at all. All 163 TARP artifacts under outputs/plots/ are pre-correction: zero contain `_submean_`, zero contain `l37`, every PS one is the old `l30-*_r100` family, and peak counts have no coverage test in any convention. No calibration/tarp/sbc file exists anywhere under ps_submean_l37, bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37 or ps_fullsky_l37. The only calibration in the corrected analysis is the score campaigns' per-cut calibration.csv at 14000 — and those are graded against `TARP < 0.15` (PLAN_score) while the VMIM gate in the same repo uses `<= 0.05 PASS / > 0.10 FAIL` (PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2). Every score row sits at 0.064-0.090: passing under one standard, inconclusive under the other, stamped "OK" either way. Worse, PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2 §8b demands the ECP curve rather than the scalar, and 7 of 39 calibration_run*.json are 100% NUL — including ps_cutall_score_l37 cut420/460/500, the non-BNT adopted-cut region. No flow checkpoints survive for the corrected campaign (0 of 45 checkpoint dirs match submean|l37), so this needs GPU retraining, not a replot.

BLOCKING 2 — the null is off truth and the gate that should catch it is toothless. At the reference point (14000 deg^2, adopted lmax=460, 5 clean pairs) the null posterior sits at Om 0.2500 / S8 0.8557 / w0 -1.0227 versus truth (0.26, 0.84, -1.0): -0.58, +0.48, -0.28 sigma off. The baryon shift being measured is +0.31, -0.74, -1.01 sigma — so in Omega_m the estimator's own null bias is about twice the baryon shift and of opposite sign. scripts/tension/qa.py sets NULL_TRUTH_NSIGMA = 5.0, tolerating a null bias 16x the effect measured, in direct contradiction of PLAN_tension_submean_l37 line 112 ("justifies a tight QA null-on-truth tolerance"). And the campaign's QA evidence for "1080 posteriors -> 1080/1080 OK, clean report" is a 519-byte, 10-row qa_report.csv covering one area and one cut, with failures.csv 100% NUL.

BLOCKING 3 — the cost of the cut is never shown, and the Fisher/NPE reconciliation reads no data. Every tension figure plots nsigma only; the campaign tables carry nsigma alone (columns: area,upper_cut,mean,std,n,n_total,n_excluded). I computed the missing number in seconds at 14000: lmax 1020 -> 460 costs sigma(S8) 0.0238 -> 0.0326 (+37%) and FoM3 41055 -> 21618, a factor 1.90 — the baryon-safe cut discards 47% of the 3-parameter FoM, and that appears nowhere in the repo. Separately, scripts/diagnostics/fisher_ratio_ladder.py — cited as the Fisher money plot — has zero np.load/read_csv/open calls: all seven bar values, the "NPE = 0.79" axvline and the 0.44-0.50 axvspan are literals, its PNG is 100% NUL, and it runs today. The two alternative reconciliation figures are a stale l100/non-submean one with its conclusion in the suptitle and a blocked input, and one whose posterior_summary input is destroyed.

CHEAP WINS on intact data. Null-on-truth vs lmax per footprint, the FoM-cost curve, and a tolerance-sensitivity inset are all minutes-long jobs on the 1836 surviving posteriors (95 MB) plus the intact agg CSV. The tolerance check came out reassuring and is worth showing precisely for that reason: across 0.2-0.5 sigma the adopted cut at 14000 moves only 420->500, and at 0.3 sigma I reproduced the paper's 860/580/540/460/380/340 exactly, confirming commit 4bc76a3's largest-safe-cut rule. I also verified the reference number itself: recomputing 3-param Q_DM at 14000/460 from 5 surviving pairs gives 0.288, matching the shipped 0.28757.

ESTIMATOR — one positive control worth banking. I ran the seed-pair Q_DM noise floor: within the null arm 0.002-0.005 sigma, within the biased arm 0.002-0.011 sigma, against 0.288 sigma for the matched comparison — a ~100x margin, so NPE training scatter does not contaminate Q_DM. What remains open is the Gaussian approximation itself: measured skew is S8 +0.135 to +0.317 and w0 -0.133 to -0.411 with |excess kurtosis| <= 0.4, same sign in both arms, so it should largely cancel in a difference of means. That is a defensible argument nobody has made; estimators.py names the missing non-Gaussian hook but no doc records it as a caveat on the result. Also: all four 6-param tables plus both 3-param pivots are 100% NUL, so the "does the 3-param projection drive it" question currently has no table behind it.

BIGGEST SCIENTIFIC GAP, and it is a framing problem more than a compute problem — one baryonification. The data tree carries exactly one baryon tag (222 files, all bare "baryonified"), no bacco/TNG/AGN/hydro variant, no varied baryon parameter, and grepping PAPER_NOTES.md and docs/README.md for baryonification / baryon model / M_c returns nothing: the model dependence is not even listed as a caveat. The adopted-lmax table is a prescription-conditional result, not a survey requirement, and must be captioned that way. Apodization is the same shape but lower stakes: 465/465 files at apod2.0, zero sensitivity tests, and no pymaster env exists to build one — a stated scope limit is the right answer.

ALREADY DOCUMENTED, not re-raised. The perm-mean observation and its consequence that error bars are training-only scatter is explicit at PLAN_tension_submean_l37 lines 110-112 (the missing piece is only a caption, not an analysis). Hartlap versus Sellentin-Heavens is thoroughly reasoned in PLAN_fisher_proper, including that the NPE never inverts a 200-sample covariance so the finite-N penalty does not apply to it. The three-stat contour sidecars already disclose seed pooling and the exact runs dropped. Uneven seed counts are flagged in HANDOFF §5 and carried in the nsigma_vs_area CSV. The one covariance item genuinely undone is the project's own validation 6 (sigma convergence vs N_perm) and validations 4-5 (MCMC equivalence): Phases I and II/III each carry a RESULT section, Phase IV carries none, so 200-perm adequacy is asserted rather than measured — and that is a clean CPU job on the six cov_rebinned_full_*.npz that survived intact.

One standing hazard for whoever acts on this: do not run scripts/monitor_tension_pilot.py against ps_submean_l37. It rewrites tension_3param_agg.csv, which is the only surviving full-seed record and the source of every adopted cut; post-damage it would re-aggregate over the thinned subset and silently move the paper's headline numbers. Archive that table first.

docs.summary:
Surveyed all of docs/ (30 md/txt), CLAUDE.md, README, plus the git log — which turned out to contain the single most recent correction, newer than any doc. The paper is a weak-lensing baryon-impact forecast on CosmoGridV1 with three summary statistics (monopole-subtracted MASTER power spectrum, starlet peak counts, starlet L1 norm), an optional BNT nulling transform, NPE inference and Gaussian Q_DM tension. Two figure families carry the paper: (1) baryon-bias tension vs scale cut, per footprint; (2) constraining power vs survey area. Everything else is methods support (Fisher forecasts, compression studies, the HOS w0-degeneracy note, the starlet-scale/ell mapping).

The project has corrected itself at least eight times and later docs retract earlier ones. The reversals that matter most, in descending order of danger if presented as current:

(a) BNT bin-1 mitigation. The shipped rebin=10 figure (`nsigma_vs_upper_cut_bnt_bin1_allareas`) showed BNT bin-1 tension flat and below 0.3 sigma, which PLAN_bnt_optimal_binning "FINAL RESULTS" retracts: raw NPE under-extracted the ill-conditioned BNT vector, inflating sigma and hiding the bias. At rebin=40 the BNT tension is 2-6x higher and converges to non-BNT at no cut, as the lossless identity requires. PLAN_score_bnt_tension_14000 then goes further with score/MOPED compression: at 14000 deg^2 the two curves TRACK, and cutting only BNT bin-1 controls the baryon tension no better than cutting all bins at the same lmax. The on-disk crossings CSVs make the reversal quantitative: at rebin=10 BNT crosses 0.3 sigma at lmax 620 vs non-BNT 500 (BNT looks better); at the corrected rebin=40 it crosses at 380 vs 500 (BNT looks worse). PAPER_NOTES section 4 still carries the pre-correction framing ("a bin-1 scale cut suffices"), and its cited source doc is destroyed (see (f)).

(b) Crossing vs adopted cut. Every doc, including PAPER_NOTES sections 0 and 2, reports the 0.3-sigma CROSSING lmax (2000:900 ... 35000:380, fullsky ~320) as if it were the cut to use. Commit 4bc76a3 (2026-07-30, newer than all docs) corrects this: the crossing is the first step-40 cut that FAILS; the adoptable cut is the last that PASSES — 860/580/540/460/380/340/300. Captioning a figure "baryon-safe" while cutting at the crossing would ship a 0.41-sigma bias at 14000.

(c) VMIM. NOTES_bnt_compression_for_paper and HANDOFF_score_tension_foldin both state VMIM learned compression FAILED (over-confident, off-truth, lossless-identity violation). PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2 RESULTS LOG (2026-06-29) reverses this: run P2f PASSES all four gates. The three root causes were jaxili instead of sbi_lens RealNVP for Stage 2, a random train/val split leaking noise realizations, and raw H0~67 detonating the flow's N(0.5,0.05) base.

(d) Fisher magnitude. The ad-hoc lstsq-over-prior Fisher's 0.37 area ratio is superseded by the local-Jacobian + estimation-noise-free covariance result, 0.45-0.48. PLAN_fisher_audit's signed-off decision to adopt the analytic NaMaster Gaussian as the PRODUCTION covariance is itself reversed by Phase I: the sim covariance carries a real 25-30% SSC/cNG excess, so the analytic Gaussian is the validator, not the production choice.

(e) A published magnitude that does not reproduce. PLAN_score_bnt_tension_14000 reports a controlled re-run of the headline campaign's own configuration at 14000/lmax1020 giving 1.43 +/- 0.30 against the published 2.22 — attributed to a high draw of raw-NPE run-to-run scatter on top of off-truth nulls (S8~0.85 vs 0.84). That number appears in PLAN_tension_submean_l37 and feeds PAPER_NOTES. Three extractions now disagree on 14000's adopted non-BNT cut: raw rebin-10 campaign 460, VMIM-compressed ~500, score-compressed 580. This is unresolved and the paper must pick one.

(f) Two documentation defects. `docs/HANDOFF_bnt_bin1_other_areas_PROGRESS.md` is 100% NUL bytes and the committed git blob is identically destroyed — unrecoverable. It is the cited source for PAPER_NOTES section 4's "bin-1 cut value scales with area" claim, which is therefore unverifiable AND pre-correction. Separately, PLAN_vmim_scalecuts.md has no results section, yet its deliverable ran on 2026-06-30 and left `plots/nsigma_vs_upper_cut_compressed_14000.png` plus a tension table — an undocumented result.

(g) Provenance rule violated at scale. The standing requirement (HANDOFF_JZ_PAPER_FIGURES section 0) is that every figure ships `_values.csv` + `_provenance.json`. `plots/` holds 140 files and ZERO sidecars, including named paper figures `nsigma_vs_upper_cut_bnt_bin1_allareas_optimal`, `nsigma_vs_upper_cut_bnt_bin1_score_14000`, `score_contours_debiased_14000` and `nsigma_vs_upper_cut_compressed_14000`. Only the 2026-07-29 regenerations under `outputs/plots/` and `outputs/diagnostics/constraining_power/` (10 figures, 20 sidecars) comply. By the project's own rule the legacy figures are unfinished.

Also destroyed and worth flagging: `plots/nsigma_vs_upper_cut_masks.pdf` and both `score_vs_raw_debiased_14000.{png,pdf}` are 100% zeros; `contours_PS_peaks_L1_baryons_BNT.pdf` is 39% zeros and, per HANDOFF section 6, cannot be honestly regenerated because the surviving BNT peaks/L1 posteriors are pre-correction (no `submean` token, BNT PS at l100).

headline_claims.claim: Raw NPE inflates BNT contours — 1.2-1.6x on masked footprints, 2.3-4.8x on the full sky — because a normalizing flow under-learns the J^T C^-1 projection on a high-dimensional, ill-conditioned, signed data vector with strong anti-correlations and information spread over many low-S/N high-ell modes. The failure is silent: the posterior stays calibrated (honestly uncertain), it is simply less informative than the data allow. Since BNT is a lossless invertible rotation, flat BNT nulls are inference-limited, not information loss.

headline_claims.claim: Score/MOPED compression — the MLE-form score theta_hat = theta_fid + F^-1 J^T C^-1 (x - mu), 6 numbers in parameter units — is a lossless sufficient statistic for a near-Gaussian likelihood (Fisher(t) = Fisher(x) to ~1e-10) and rescues the BNT vector. It realizes a 1.46x BNT/non-BNT FoM3 advantage at 14000 (rebin=20, fixed cut), calibrated and on truth, versus 0.96x for whitening. The F^-1 rotation into parameter units is essential: the raw score J^T C^-1 x has condition number ~1e8 and the NPE fails on it.

headline_claims.superseded_note: REVERSED by docs/PLAN_bnt_vmim_v2.md RESULTS LOG (2026-06-29): the corrected pipeline PASSES. Run P2f gives identity |Delta mean|/sigma = [0.14, 0.15, 0.03], both bases on truth (BNT S8 0.846, non-BNT 0.843), TARP <= 0.06, SBC rank-std 0.30-0.31, and Omega_m/S8 on the Fisher floor. So the paper should NOT state that learned compression failed; it should state that a correctly-built VMIM independently reproduces the score result, which removes the score's 'by construction' caveat. 1. **`build_bnt_bin1_fullsky_plot.py`** (undocumented). The annotation box says *"0.05→1.10 (22× better) but still only 29% of the non-BNT/lossless value (3.83)"*. And the `0.05` baseline came from `bnt_ps_bin1_fullsky_l37/tables/tension_3param_agg.csv`, which is **100% NUL bytes** — so "22× better" has no recoverable source.

3. **`plot_score_contours_debiased.py`** — `--bnt-cut 460` is the **crossing** (0.304σ, already failing), not the adoptable cut. I computed both from the score tables: BNT largest-safe = **420**, non-BNT = 580. A figure captioned "at the de-biasing scale cut" compares a failing BNT cut to a passing non-BNT cut, biasing the FoM ratio toward BNT.

`EXTRACTED_R40` itself I re-verified: BNT-r40/nonBNT-r10 at ℓmax 1020 = 56.5/64.5/65.0/75.8/98.6/99.1 % vs the annotated 87/85/82/76/93/93 — only 14000 coincides, exactly as documented.

## Method

Probed every posterior-like `.npy` under `outputs/samples/` and `outputs/baryon_tension/` (plus `score_experiment/`, `diagnostics/`, `npe_results/`) with a real `np.load(mmap_mode='r')` header test plus a strided all-zero/non-finite content probe: **10,923 files, 9,094 READABLE, 1,828 CORRUPT (all `ValueError`), 1 NONFINITE**. 1,574 of the 1,828 corrupt files carry mtime 2026-07-22, confirming the re-transfer signature. Pairing was validated against an independent source: my paired-run sets reproduce exactly the `runs`/`runs_dropped` lists inside `outputs/plots/contours_three_stats/contours_PS_peaks_L1_both_14000_provenance.json` (PS 14000@1020 → runs [1,3,4,5]; peaks → [2,4,5,6,7,9,10]; L1 → [2,4,6,7]).

## The four beliefs you asked me to check

1. **PS submean lmin=37, 5 seeds × 6 footprints × 18 step-40 cuts — CONFIRMED**, and there is *more* than believed: footprint 14000 additionally carries a full **step-20** grid (36 cuts including 1000 and 1024), and there is a sparse rebin=40 branch. But the damage is severe and lopsided: only **36 of 108** step-40 cells still have all 5 matched pairs, and at the adopted cuts you have 3/4/4/5/4/5 pairs (2000/5000/10000/14000/28000/35000), fullsky@300 = 3.

2. **peaks scales234 submean, 1 seed per footprint, 3 of 12 destroyed — CONFIRMED exactly.** The important correction is *which* 3: 14000-biased, 28000-null, 35000-null. So only **3 of 6 footprints (2000, 5000, 10000) retain a matched pair**, and the reference Stage-IV footprint 14000 has **none**. A 6-point baryon-safe peaks-vs-area figure is not buildable from disk. `scales2345` (drops finest, keeps coarse) is a possible fallback — it retains pairs at 2000/5000/10000/**14000**.

3. **L1 scales234 submean does not exist at all — CONFIRMED.** Zero files match `scales234` + `_submean_` anywhere. The 305 figure is right: 291 L1 + 14 BNT L1 `scales234` posteriors exist, all pre-correction. **Good news that changes the plan:** this is a run that was never launched, not a casualty. Every input needed to launch it is present and 100% readable in `stage3_forecast` — 28 submean L1 training grids, and 56 submean fiducials covering both `nobaryons` and `baryonified` at all six footprints. The blocker is GPU time, not data.

4. **BNT PS exists at submean/l37; BNT peaks/L1 only pre-correction — CONFIRMED.** All 86 BNT L1 and all 12 BNT peaks files are non-submean. BNT PS is in fact the richest corrected product (r10 and a full independent r40 sweep).

## Corrections and things not in the brief

- **The adopted-cut list is verified, not assumed.** Recomputing "largest step-40 lmax with mean < 0.3σ" from the surviving `ps_submean_l37/tables/tension_3param_agg.csv` reproduces 860/580/540/460/380/340 exactly, and `ps_fullsky_l37` gives 300. The crossings are one step higher in every case.

- **The tables are the only surviving record of the full-seed result.** Every agg table records `n=5` (or 9 for VMIM) with `n_excluded=0`, but the posteriors on disk no longer support that. `ps_submean_l37` 3-param and both `bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37` table sets are **not reproducible** from what remains.

- **Zero-length is the wrong test for the damaged tables — there are no zero-length CSVs at all.** 38 CSVs are the right size on disk and 100% NUL. `pandas.read_csv` returns 0 rows and a single `Unnamed: 0` column without raising, so an existence-or-size check passes and the panel comes out empty. Worst cases: **all eight files in `bnt_ps_bin1_fullsky_l37/tables/`** (only `tables_r60/` survives), and in `ps_submean_l37/tables/` the **entire 6-param family plus both 3-param pivots** (3param agg + long survive). Also destroyed: `bnt_ps_bin1_submean_l37/qa/qa_report.csv`, `ps_submean_l37/qa/failures.csv`, and 22 files in `outputs/tension_analysis/`. Separately, 4 legacy CSVs are a bare newline (mtime January — genuine empty writes, not RAID damage) and `vmim_v2/native480/tension_native480.csv` is header-only.

- **The compressed branch is in the corrected convention, verified from source** — `scripts/jz/dump_score_caches.slurm` uses `--subtract-mean --lower-cut 37 --rebin 20`. But its own artifacts don't record that: `cache.npz` holds only `theta, x, x_fid`, so the convention is unattributable from outputs alone.

- **The compressed/VMIM sweep is broken precisely at the adopted cut**: `nonbnt_c460` retains **0 of 9** matched pairs while its table claims `n_seeds=9`. `bnt_c460` = 2/9.

- **The six-footprint adopted-cut montage source is half gone**: 7 of 15 `npe_score/posterior_summary_*` files destroyed, hitting bnt_580 at 2000/28000/35000 and nonbnt_460 at 5000/35000.

- **`score_experiment/npe_whiten` is null-only** — all 21 files are `nobaryons_vs_nobaryons`. It can never support a bias figure regardless of damage.

- **Regeneration paths differ sharply.** The 48 non-`r10` score caches pass a zip-CRC test, so `vmim_v2/scalecuts` is rerunnable; but all 4 `vmim/cache` (v1) caches are damaged (`nonbnt_460` is `BadZipFile`) and the 4 `*_full_r10_14000_*` caches have CRC errors.

- **Nonstandard mask tag**: stale L1 at the 2000 footprint splits across `masked_2001sqdeg` (20 files, 3 pairs) and `masked_2002sqdeg` (46 files, 17 pairs). Anything keyed only on AREA+1 will silently drop most of that footprint.

## Provenance rule — a real defect at scale

Only **10 figures in the entire repo** carry `_values.csv` + `_provenance.json`; all 10 are intact and are genuinely good (they even record `runs_dropped` with "unreadable on one side"). Against ~9,536 figures, and with **1,558 of 9,404** figures in `outputs/` being 100% NUL, that leaves the overwhelming majority unfinished by the project's own standard. No `tables*/` directory anywhere has a sidecar. And the four campaign `manifest.json` files are **not** campaign manifests — each records only the last sbatch invocation (`ps_submean_l37` claims `areas=[28000], upper_cuts=[1020], runs=[6..10]`), so they cannot be used as the authoritative inventory.

## What is actually ready to build from

READY: peaks `scales1234` submean (5–10 pairs/footprint), L1 `scales1234` submean (4–9), the stale-but-deep peaks/L1 `scales234` sets, and the intact BNT PS + fullsky PS tables. Everything else is PARTIAL, and the paper's baryon-safe NPE figure needs one L1 `scales234` submean run plus 3 peaks `scales234` submean re-runs — all inputs verified present.
